arxiv-1701-01282.title: On completely regular and Clifford ordered semigroups
arxiv-1701-01282.creator: A. K. Bhuniya and K. Hansda Department of Mathematics, Visva-Bharati University,Santiniketan, Bolpur - 731235, West Bengal, India, anjankbhuniya@gmail.com, kalyanh4@gmail.com
arxiv-1701-01282.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by A. K. Bhuniya and K. Hansda Department of Mathematics, Visva-Bharati University,Santiniketan, Bolpur - 731235, West Bengal, India, anjankbhuniya@gmail.com, kalyanh4@gmail.com. Lee and Kwon [ 12 ] defined an ordered semigroup S S to be completely regular if a ∈ ( a 2 S a 2 ] a\in(a^{2}Sa^{2}] for every a ∈ S a\in S . We characterize every completely regular ordered semigroup as a union of t t -simple subsemigroups, and every Clifford ordered semigroup as a complete semilattice of t t -simple subsemigroups.

arxiv-2106-06540.title: Galactic Clustering Under Power-law Modified Newtonian Potential
arxiv-2106-06540.creator: Abdul W. Khanday, Sudhaker Upadhyay, Prince A. Ganai
arxiv-2106-06540.description: Abstract We estimate galaxy clustering under a modified gravitational potential. In particular, the modifications in gravitational potential energy occur due to a power-law and cosmological constant terms. We derive a canonical partition function for the system of galaxies interacting under such a modified gravitational potential. Moreover, we compute various thermodynamical equation of states for the system.

arxiv-2106-14781.title: The curvature of convex sum of metrics and applications
arxiv-2106-14781.creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Llohann D. Sperança
arxiv-2106-14781.description: Abstract In this paper we explore the curvature of convex sums of Riemannian metrics g ⁡ ( t ) = ( 1 − t ) ​ g 0 + t ​ g 1 g(t)=(1-t)g_{0}+tg_{1} , and study whether such a deformation can increase the curvature of an immersed totally geodesic flat tori.

arxiv-2205-09862.title: Recurrent segmentation meets block models in temporal networks
arxiv-2205-09862.creator: Chamalee Wickrama Arachchi, Nikolaj Tatti
arxiv-2205-09862.description: Abstract A popular approach to model interactions is to represent them as a network with nodes being the agents and the interactions being the edges. Interactions are often timestamped, which leads to having timestamped edges. Many real-world temporal networks have a recurrent or possibly cyclic behaviour. For example, social network activity may be heightened during certain hours of day.

arxiv-2401-03268.title: Adaptive Randomization Methods for Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trials (SMARTs) via Thompson Sampling
arxiv-2401-03268.creator: Peter Norwood 1,∗, Marie Davidian 2∗∗, and Eric Laber 3∗∗∗ 1 Quantum Leap Healthcare Collaborative, San Francisco, California, U.S.A. 2 Department of Statistics, North Carolina State University, Raleigh, North Carolina, U.S.A. 3 Department of Statistical Science, Duke University, Durham, North Carol
arxiv-2401-03268.description: Abstract Response-adaptive randomization (RAR) has been studied extensively in conventional, single-stage clinical trials, where it has been shown to yield ethical and statistical benefits, especially in trials with many treatment arms. However, RAR and its potential benefits are understudied in sequential multiple assignment randomized trials (SMARTs), which are the gold-standard trial design for evaluation of multi-stage treatment regimes.

arxiv-2404-06028.title: Correlation decoupling of Casimir interaction in an electrolyte driven by external electric fields
arxiv-2404-06028.creator: Guangle Du, David S. Dean, Bing Miao, Rudolf Podgornik
arxiv-2404-06028.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guangle Du, David S. Dean, Bing Miao, Rudolf Podgornik. It is well established that the long range van der Waals or thermal Casimir interaction between two semi-infinite dielectrics separated by a distance H H is screened by an intervening electrolyte. Here we show how this interaction is modified when an electric field of strength E E is applied parallel to the dielectric boundaries, leading to a non-equilibrium steady state with a current.

arxiv-2412-11810.title: Optimal Gradient Checkpointing for Sparse and Recurrent Architectures using Off-Chip Memory
arxiv-2412-11810.creator: Wadjih Bencheikh*, Jan Finkbeiner*, Emre Neftci
arxiv-2412-11810.description: Abstract Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are valued for their computational efficiency and reduced memory requirements on tasks involving long sequence lengths but require high memory-processor bandwidth to train. Checkpointing techniques can reduce the memory requirements by only storing a subset of intermediate states, the checkpoints, but are still rarely used due to the computational overhead of the additional recomputation phase.

arxiv-2502-11786.title: A method for signal components identification in acoustic signal with non-Gaussian background noise using clustering of data in time-frequency domain.
arxiv-2502-11786.creator: Anita Drewnicka, Anna Michalak, Radosław Zimroz, Anil Kumar, Agnieszka Wyłomańska, Jacek Wodecki
arxiv-2502-11786.description: Abstract The problem of damage detection based on noisy vibration/acoustic signal analysis is well understood by researchers when the observed noise comes from the Gaussian distribution. However, if there are random impulsive and wideband disturbances in the measured data, the task becomes more difficult.

arxiv-2504-00319.title: Methodology for Detecting Energy Anomalies due to Multi-Replay Attacks on Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
arxiv-2504-00319.creator: Sagar Babu Mitikiri, Vedantham Lakshmi Srinivas, Mayukha Pal
arxiv-2504-00319.description: Abstract The increasing deployment of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructures (EVCIs) introduces cybersecurity challenges, particularly due to inherent vulnerabilities, making them susceptible to cyberattacks. The vulnerable points in EVCI are charging ports, which serve as the links between the EVs and the EVCI as they transfer the data along with the power.

arxiv-2505-02976.title: The Disks In Scorpius-Centaurus Survey (DISCS) I: Four Newly-Resolved Debris Disks in Polarized Intensity Light Facilities: Gemini:South, ESO:VLT
arxiv-2505-02976.creator: Justin Hom, Thomas M. Esposito, Katie A. Crotts, Gaspard Duchêne, Jennifer Patience, Johan Mazoyer, Robert J. De Rosa, Christine H. Chen, Paul Kalas, Bruce Macintosh, Brenda C. Matthews
arxiv-2505-02976.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Justin Hom, Thomas M. Esposito, Katie A. Crotts, Gaspard Duchêne, Jennifer Patience, Johan Mazoyer, Robert J. De Rosa, Christine H. Chen, Paul Kalas, Bruce Macintosh, Brenda C. Matthews. The presence of infrared excesses around stars directly correlates to spatially-resolved imaging detections of circumstellar disks at both mm and optical/near-infrared wavelengths. High contrast imagers have resolved dozens of circumstellar disks with scattered light polarimetric imaging.

arxiv-2510-12038.title: Feynman Formula for Discrete-time Quantum Walks Thanks: Email for Fouque: fouque@pstat.ucsb.edu Thanks: Email for Ichiba: ichiba@pstat.ucsb.edu Thanks: Email for Lam: kalok@ucsb.edu
arxiv-2510-12038.creator: Jean-Pierre Fouque, Tomoyuki Ichiba, Ka Lok Lam
arxiv-2510-12038.description: Abstract . We explicitly connect (discrete-time) quantum walks on ℤ \mathbb{Z} with a four-state Markov additive process via a Feynman-type formula ( 2.13 ). Using this representation, we derive a relation between the spectral decomposition of the Markov additive process and the limiting density of the homogeneous quantum walk.

arxiv-2511-19258.title: CARV, ICS, FORTH              B.Sc. Thesis by A. Psistakis              CSD, UoC
arxiv-2511-19258.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . \addchaptertocentry Abstract In complex systems with many compute nodes consisting of many CPUs, that are coherent inside each node, one issue is to achieve coherence between them in an efficient and valid way. Unimem system [ 1 ] addresses this issue and in order to support it, it suggests a virtualized system (virtual global address space) that is able to handle this. This approach requires the use of the I/O Memory Management Unit (IOMMU) in each node.

arxiv-2512-22008.title: Rethinking photonic nanojets: a new definition and design paradigm
arxiv-2512-22008.creator: Mirza Karamehmedović, Kristoffer Linder-Steinlein, Jesper Glückstad
arxiv-2512-22008.description: Abstract We propose a rigorous, physically interpretable, and quantifiable definition of the photonic nanojet (PNJ). This framework resolves longstanding ambiguities in measuring PNJ dimensions and leverages an optimal mass transport-based metric to quantify PNJ quality. Building on this metric, we develop a PNJ steering methodology that requires no opto-mechanical intervention, relying solely on phase-only illumination modulation.

arxiv-2604-03384.creator: Andre Bacellar

europmc-pmc4566946.title: Cumulative meta-analysis of interleukins 6 and 1β, tumour necrosis factor α and C-reactive protein in patients with major depressive disorder.
europmc-pmc4566946.creator: Haapakoski R, Mathieu J, Ebmeier KP, Alenius H, Kivimäki M.
europmc-pmc4566946.description: Cumulative meta-analyses are used to evaluate the extent to which further studies are needed to confirm or refute a hypothesis. We used this approach to assess observational evidence on systemic inflammation in individuals with major depressive disorder. We identified 58 studies

pmc-10629137.title: Impacts of different triathlon races on systemic cytokine profile and metabolic parameters in healthy individuals: a systematic review
pmc-10629137.creator: Matheus Santos de Sousa Fernandes, Jefferson Mariano Gomes, Felipe J. Aidar, Mabliny Thuany, Tayrine Ordonio Filgueira, Raphael Fabrício de Souza, Georgian Badicu, Fatma Hilal Yagin, Gianpiero Greco, Stefania Cataldi, Angela Castoldi, Abdullah F. Alghannam, Fabrício Oliveira Souto
pmc-10629137.description: The present systematic review aimed to discuss the impacts of different triathlon protocols on the level of pro and anti-inflammatory cytokines, as well as biomarkers related to the performance of healthy individuals. Four databases [PubMed (28 articles), Scopus (24 articles), Science Direct (200 articles), and SPORT Discus (1101 articles) were assessed.

pmc-11449749.title: Chronic kidney diseases and inflammation research: a bibliometric analysis
pmc-11449749.creator: Heyong Wang, Yang Chen, Yujuan Gou, Dianxing Yang, Lanyue Xiong
pmc-11449749.description: BackgroundChronic kidney diseases (CKD) is a severe public health problem. This study aimed to explore the field of inflammation-related research in CKD from a bibliometric perspective.MethodsRelevant literature published between 2004 and 2023 were searched from the Web of Science database. The bibliometric analysis were performed to summarize countries, institutions, authors, journals and keywords using VOSviewer and CiteSpace.

pmc-11454967.title: 6978 Traumatic Presentation Of A Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor
pmc-11454967.creator: C J Kahn, J Mai, A E Cabrera, A D Anderson, D H Huynh
pmc-11454967.description: Disclosure: C.J. Kahn: None. J. Mai: None. A.E. Cabrera: None. A.D. Anderson: None. D.H. Huynh: None. Background: Insulinomas are a subset of functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors associated with neuroglycopenic symptoms, fasting hypoglycemia, and rapid resolution of symptoms with glucose administration. Despite this classic presentation, patients often spend years undiagnosed before formal diagnosis and definitive management.

pmc-11488171.title: Explainable artificial intelligence and domain adaptation for predicting HIV infection with graph neural networks
pmc-11488171.creator: Evan Yu, Jingcheng Du, Yang Xiang, Xinyue Hu, Jingna Feng, Xi Luo, John A. Schneider, Degui Zhi, Kayo Fujimoto, Cui Tao
pmc-11488171.description: ObjectiveInvestigation of explainable deep learning methods for graph neural networks to predict HIV infections with social network information and performing domain adaptation to evaluate model transferability across different datasets.MethodsNetwork data from two cohorts of younger sexual minority men (SMM) from two U.S. cities (Chicago, IL, and Houston, TX) were collected between 2014 and 2016.

pmc-11626331.title: Comparison of Complications of Non‐Resorbable (Permanent) Fillers and Resorbable Fillers
pmc-11626331.creator: Tom S Decates, Valerie Vroege, Merel A Hamer, Peter Velthuis
pmc-11626331.description: ssue fillers, for the purpose of adverse event description they are mostly classified by their biodegradability into non‐resorbable (permanent) and resorbable fillers [2]. Permanent fillers remain in situ indefinitely. These have been used in the past for many years but have been banned in many countries in the past years (in the Netherlands since 2015) [3].

pmc-11673377.title: LncRNAs Involved in Antioxidant Response Regulation as Biomarkers of Gestational Diabetes: A Study on H19, MALAT1 and MEG3
pmc-11673377.creator: Jovana Stevanović, Uroš Petrović, Ana Penezić, Ognjen Radojičić, Daniela Ardalić, Milica Mandić, Vesna Mandić-Marković, Željko Miković, Miloš Brkušanin, Olgica Nedić, Zorana Dobrijević, Paola Venditti
pmc-11673377.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent findings highlighted the potential of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as novel indicators of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), as they demonstrate altered expression in metabolic disorders, oxidative stress (OS) and inflammation (IFM). The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic potential and prognostic significance of the OS/IFM-related lncRNAs H19, MALAT1 and MEG3 in GDM and their correlations with redox status-related parameters.

pmc-12532673.title: Virtual-reality induced nostalgia: Duration and psychological benefits
pmc-12532673.creator: İrem Yılmaz-Özdemir, Tim Wildschut, Constantine Sedikides, Erich W. Graf
pmc-12532673.description: We developed a new nostalgia induction using virtual reality. We compared this virtual reality task (VRT) with the established event reflection task (ERT) in terms of intensity of felt nostalgia and strength of psychological benefits produced by each induction method (Experiment 1) and the durability of these effects over time (Experiment 2).

pmc-12551021.title: From Gamma Rays to Green Light: Comparative Efficacy of Indocyanine Green and Technetium-99m in Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy for Breast Cancer
pmc-12551021.creator: Vlad Alexandru Gâta, Radu Alexandru Ilieș, Nicoleta Zenovia Antone, Roxana Pintican, Codruț Cosmin Nistor-Ciurba, Ștefan Țîțu, Alex Victor Orădan, Maximilian Vlad Muntean, Gheorghe Gerald Filip, Alexandru Irimie, Patriciu Andrei Achimaș-Cadariu
pmc-12551021.description: Background/Objectives: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is currently the standard approach for axillary staging in breast cancer. Conventional techniques are radioisotope-based (Technetium-99m, Tc99m) and remain widely used, but novel tracers like Indocyanine Green (ICG) fluorescence provide potential advantages regarding feasibility and logistics.

pmc-12573933.title: Insulin resistance surrogates predict major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12573933.creator: Feng Wang, Wendi Huang, Zhuoquan Wang, Di Zhang, Hongyang Qiao, Nianshao Chen, Xiaoqiu Ni, Jinguo Cheng, Weicheng Ni
pmc-12573933.description: BackgroundHeart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently coexist and portend a poor prognosis. Insulin resistance (IR) is implicated in cardiorenal pathophysiology, but practical surrogate IR indices for predicting risk in this high-risk and understudied population are lacking.

pmc-13316694.creator: You Jin Lee, Jae Hyun Park, Hee Ju Nam, Soon-Chan Kim, Min Jung Kim, Seung-Yong Jeong, Ji Won Park, Ja-Lok Ku

pmc-13462252.title: To Investigate the Impact and Potential Benefits of Integrating Proms Into Routine ICU Care for Patients with Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) Superimposed on Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Undergoing Hemodialysis
pmc-13462252.creator: Akash P Datir, Tanima Baronia, Durgesh Makwana
pmc-13462252.description: IntroductionChronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a widespread public health concern associated with increased mortality, morbidity, impaired quality of life, and considerable healthcare costs. A particularly challenging subset includes patients with Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) superimposed on CKD, especially those undergoing hemodialysis, due to their high risks of mortality, hospitalization, and progression of underlying CKD.

pmc-13572153.title: Functional impairment profiles and long-term care implications among community health service-managed older adults with disability in China: a latent profile and network analysis study
pmc-13572153.creator: Ruishan Liu, Yiheng Chen, Ting Niu, Dingyi Zhang, Yuelin Li, Yulin Lu, Dan Yang
pmc-13572153.description: ObjectiveTo identify functional impairment profiles among older adults with disability managed within a community health service catchment in China and examine classification-adjusted associations between living arrangement and profile membership.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 361 older adults with disability from 13 communities in Kunming, China, surveyed from January to March 2026.

pmc-13582950.title: Strengthening diagnostic capacity for viral hemorrhagic fevers in Forest Guinea: advances in Lassa fever case detection
pmc-13582950.creator: Fara Raymond Koundouno, Youssouf Sidibe, Saa Lucien Millimono, Kékoura Ifono, Julia Hinzmann, Hugo Soubrier, Karifa Kourouma, Tamba Elie Millimouno, Fernand M’Bemba Tolno, Faya Moriba Kamano, Mamadou Dioulde Barry, Soua Koulemou, Bely Sonomy, Mariame Traore, Kaba Keïta, Mette Hinrichs, Sarah Ryter,
pmc-13582950.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) remain a major public health threat in resource-limited settings. The 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic exposed critical gaps in laboratory preparedness and diagnostic capacity in most-at-risk countries, including Guinea. In order to implement sustainable in-country laboratory capacity for early detection and rapid response to VHF outbreaks, a decentralized diagnostics laboratory strengthening program started in the forested region of Guinea in Guéckédou (2017) and N’Zérékoré (2021).
